scope: 17 existing highest-impact debate owners; 85 Catholic-side argumentative stages reviewed against exact source passages for bounded doctrinal content, context and necessary inference. Not full certification of every stage sentence or clinical/historical premise.
rules: The status PRIMARY_NORM_SUPPORTED_WITH_QUALIFICATIONS means the core doctrinal claim has a verified passage; it does not certify every clause or ancillary assertion.
REASONED_APPLICATION and SYNTHESIS_NOT_QUOTATION identify authorial argument, not source quotations.
English and French source rendering requires separate native bilingual approval.
Clinical, historic, philosophical or pastoral ancillary assertions beyond the principal original source remain unapproved.

cases.source_scope_caveat: The instruction addresses theologians specifically, not every lay disagreement; personal sincerity is not autonomous doctrinal authority.

stages.bounded_finding: Personal conscience obligation is a separate traditional premise not established by Donum Veritatis alone.
§28 explicitly refuses making a theologian's subjective conscience an autonomous doctrinal judge.
§§28–30 support patient reflection and openness to correction; broader conscience formation is synthesis.
§§29–31 support patient inquiry, loyal difficulties and private recourse to authority.
The conclusion applies document principles; it is not itself a papal quotation.

cases.source_scope_caveat: A theological school's dissent cannot be treated as competing magisterial authority.

stages.bounded_finding: Genuine contested subjects are recognized at §§24–25; number of dissenters alone is no criterion.
§23 distinguishes definitive and non-definitive teachings; §28 rejects autonomous doctrinal authority.
The text does permit serious difficulty without making that theological difficulty public-license dissent.
§§28–31 require serious inquiry, recourse to competent authority and loyal openness.
Final synthesis is reasoned from §§23–31, not individually declared infallible.

cases.source_scope_caveat: A betrothal is not marriage; canonical form ordinarily applies, with legally specified exceptions.

stages.bounded_finding: Engaged love is a prudential concession, not a juridical marriage fact.
Canon 1057 requires consent directed to present marriage, not future intention alone.
Canon 1057 and 1108 support distinction; 1116 and 1127 show non-universal form exceptions.
Contraception example calls for Casti/Humanae Vitae, not can.1057 alone.
Conclusion depends on conjugal anthropology beyond the Code's bare legal text.

cases.source_scope_caveat: The canon distinguishes sterility from antecedent perpetual impotence; it does not alone prove a full philosophy of marriage.

stages.bounded_finding: Friendship and fidelity among persons are acknowledged, not disproved by canon law.
Meaning of marriage draws on Christian anthropology, not solely impediments.
The doctrinal account of marriage needs Casti/CDF2003 alongside the canon.
§1 and §3 confirm different legal status of impotence and sterility.
The account of conjugal complementarity is a philosophical synthesis, not a quote from §3.

cases.source_scope_caveat: Sterility does not prohibit/annul marriage; impotence does under specified legal conditions.

stages.bounded_finding: §3 directly verifies sterility is not an impediment.
Different procreative outcomes and bodily act are analytically distinct.
§1 vs §3 explicitly distinguishes antecedent perpetual impotence and sterility.
Defense of what counts as conjugal union requires an additional argument.
Final legal distinction is supported; moral anthropology is not established by canon alone.

cases.source_scope_caveat: The text affirms offspring, marriage's unity, marital love and mutual perfecting; recognize §24's broad-versus-restricted ends distinction.

stages.bounded_finding: §§23–24 establish positive spousal love and mutual help.
Opposition between procreation and love is a constructed false dichotomy.
§§11–17 cover children; §19 fidelity; §§23–25 love and mutual improvement.
Childlessness does not erase married love; the text does not promise universal fertility.
Broad purposes and narrower primary end require context, not flattening into one formula.

cases.source_scope_caveat: Do not generalize canon 1141 to every valid marriage; safety separation under 1153 is explicit.

stages.bounded_finding: Canon 1153 permits separation for grave danger.
§1151 and §1141 distinguish living together and matrimonial bond.
1141 absolute rule applies to ratified-consummated marriage; 1142–50 specify other dissolutions.
1153 §1 explicitly permits leaving without prior decree where delay is dangerous.
The conclusion must preserve safety, especially abuse and children.

cases.source_scope_caveat: Canon law distinguishes impediment of a prior bond, invalid marriage, and exceptional dissolution.

stages.bounded_finding: Separation rights require separate can.1153, not divorce alone.
Can.1085 §2 requires nullity/dissolution securely established before new union.
§§1142–1150 concern special dissolution; nullity is not dissolution.
Civil divorce's legal effects differ by jurisdiction; prior sacramental bond remains.
Do not treat all civil divorces as canonical dissolution or all cases as declarations of nullity.

cases.source_scope_caveat: Spousal consent does not suspend divine law or conjugal fidelity.

stages.bounded_finding: The benefits of marital intimacy are substantial; §23 positively treats love.
§§19–21 forbid transferring conjugal rights to outsiders by mutual agreement.
§§19–23 support exclusivity; Humanae Vitae addresses integrity of the act.
Unrestricted consent alone is not moral analysis; this is an application.
Final balance of fidelity and chosen moral object is synthesis.

cases.original_passage_locator: §13; see Aquinas Supplement q.64 a.1 ad 2 and CIC 1153
cases.source_scope_caveat: The papal text expressly judges an imposed conjugal act without regard to spouse's condition and reasonable wishes not genuine love.

stages.bounded_finding: Some reciprocal duties are recognized by Aquinas, not established by HV §13.
A duty of marital fidelity is not force authorization; grounded in HV §13.
HV §13 and CIC 1153 together reject coercion and permit safety separation.
Against manipulative refusal is pastoral inference, not wording of HV §13.
Summary preserves real rights while forbidding coercion.

cases.source_scope_caveat: Direct frustration of the conjugal act is condemned even when avoiding pregnancy has grave motives.

stages.bounded_finding: Serious reasons for spacing are explicit in HV §16.
§§53–56 distinguish direct frustration from permitted continence.
Casti §§53–56 condemn frustration; HV §§12–15 specify contraceptive object/therapeutic distinction.
Intention to avoid pregnancy alone does not justify deliberately contraceptive act.
Conclusion is normative synthesis, not scientific fertility claim.

cases.original_passage_locator: §§14–16; see Pius XII 1951 address, paragraphs on periodi agenesici
cases.source_scope_caveat: Same end of avoiding pregnancy does not make contracepted intercourse and periodic abstinence the same moral object.

stages.bounded_finding: §16 explicitly acknowledges intention to avoid children in both cases.
§§14 and 16 distinguish means, not just desired outcome.
HV §16 and Pius XII's Italian original support the essential distinction and serious-reasons condition.
Claims about misuse are grounded in Pius XII's sufficiency-of-motives discussion.
Conclusion is argument from differing choices, not clinical effectiveness of NFP.

cases.original_passage_locator: 29 October 1951 address, Italian original: from 'Si presenta inoltre oggigiorno' through 'gravi motivi'
cases.source_scope_caveat: Pius XII distinguishes regulating use of marital right from restricting the right in matrimonial consent and requires sufficient reasons.

stages.bounded_finding: Not every periodic abstinence pattern is justified; sufficient motives matter.
Contraception changes a performed act; abstinence changes which acts occur.
Pius XII recognizes rights-vs-use distinction, including possible consent invalidity.
Conjugal chosen-object analysis must also cite HV §§14–16.
Distinction predates modern NFP claims and remains context-dependent.

cases.source_scope_caveat: The encyclical narrowly excuses the reluctant spouse acting for grave reason who seeks charitably to dissuade the other.

stages.bounded_finding: Do not assume equal responsibility of willing and unwilling spouse.
Cooperation assessment depends on individual intention and circumstances.
§59 states grave reason, reluctance and charitable efforts to dissuade.
§59 does not pronounce contraceptive choice licit; it limits culpability.
Some complex material-cooperation cases require further moralist analysis.

cases.source_scope_caveat: Even embryo-sparing homologous IVF replaces rather than assists the conjugal act; treatments aiding fertility are distinguished.

stages.bounded_finding: DP §§12–13 affirm permissible fertility treatment; not every technology excluded.
The document specifies replacing versus assisting the conjugal act.
Donum Vitae II.B.5 even rejects embryo-sparing IVF; DP §§12–16 extends context.
Couple's legitimate desire does not by itself justify all means; original explicitly says so.
Do not imply children conceived via IVF have diminished dignity.

cases.original_passage_locator: II.A.3 and end of II.B; see Dignitas Personae §13
cases.source_scope_caveat: Surrogacy judged illicit due to separation of gestation and parental duties, independent of whether payment occurs.

stages.bounded_finding: Good motivation recognized; motive does not change the chosen surrogacy arrangement.
Unpaid surrogacy also engages the document's separation concern.
II.A.3 directly condemns surrogacy but defines two particular variants.
Adoption is endorsed separately (end of Donum Vitae II.B and DP §13); moral distinction is reasoned.
Specific modern reproductive configurations require matching to original definitions.

cases.original_passage_locator: 11 July 2009 clarification, passage citing Pius XII's 27 Nov 1951 address
cases.source_scope_caveat: CDF distinguishes intended direct fetal killing from legitimate maternal disease treatment with unintended fetal death; source cannot certify all ectopic treatment methods.

stages.bounded_finding: Urgent hemorrhage and treatment needs are clinical facts requiring ACOG or equivalent, not CDF.
The moral distinction is explicitly in CDF clarification and contemporary committee statement.
CDF itself teaches therapeutic distinction; medical method classification is separately debated.
Distinguishing intention from foreseen effects rests in doctrinal text; procedural choices need further examination.
Do not delay emergency treatment over unresolved moralist disagreement.
